subject: Capacity cliff: reserved-throughput shortfall impacting ClearBridge — exec triage
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@clearbridge.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@clearbridge.com
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden 5xx and latency spike — reserved throughput not honoring commit

Rafael,

We started seeing sustained 5xx errors and token latency blowups across our production inference routes this morning around 08:45 PDT. Our monitoring shows a ~65% drop in sustained throughput against the reserved commit (we're on a Reserved plan, contract DB-9421). Errors are concentrated on the /v1/generate route and we're getting frequent OOM-style 5xxs at peak.

Attached: clearbridge_ops_log_2026-08-15.txt (sample logs), detailed_kpi_snapshot.csv (minute-level metrics 08:30-10:00).

Impact: checkout flows failing for some merchants, increased error rates triggering our own incident alerts. This is already customer-facing. Please escalate — we need either immediate capacity relief or a clear mitigation plan and ETA.

Can Redwood allocate emergency dedicated capacity or enable a temporary fallback (quantized model or reduced concurrency) while we triage? We also need to know if this will affect our SLA credits.

Aisha
Head of Core Ops, ClearBridge Financial

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: aisha.khan@clearbridge.com
Date: 2026-08-15T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Capacity cliff — technical triage notes (pool metrics attached)

Quick triage notes from the infra side (attaching pool_metrics_snapshot.png):

Findings:
- The GPU pool backing ClearBridge's reservation (pool-3) shows sustained 92% GPU utilization across 4 nodes starting ~08:40.
- KV cache eviction rate spiked dramatically at 08:38 -> frequent KV reloads causing latency amplification for long-context requests.
- Several small tenants routing heavy short requests created noisy-neighbor interference; per-tenant quota enforcement was not applied due to an orchestration lag.

Immediate mitigations I will apply now:
- Apply per-tenant rate limiter for ClearBridge to cap throughput to their reserved commit while we bring up headroom (limits: concurrency=2, max_tokens=512).
- Turn on prefix KV caching for the customer's top-10 request patterns to reduce reloads.
- Re-provision +2 GPUs from the shared rapid-burst pool to pool-3 (this requires exec OK for non-standard allocation).
- Schedule a rolling restart of the serving nodes in pool-3 in 30 minutes to flush the cache churn and reset kernel memory.

If we can get exec authorization for the re-provisioning I will enact the capacity move and confirm when both the rate limits and kv-prefix caching are live.

-David
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Team — following the incident yesterday, we need an explicit exec decision so we can (a) reallocate +2 GPUs to pool-3 for the next 6 hours, (b) approve a one-time customer credit for ClearBridge equivalent to 12 hours of their reserved throughput, and (c) authorize a procurement fast-path to increase their reserved commit by 25% while the postmortem is concluded.

Why this is outside normal policy: the noisy-neighbor and KV eviction pattern produced a capacity cliff that the standard burst runway cannot absorb. David's mitigations are ready to run, but the GPU move requires CVM authorization.

Proposed approvals (please reply with APPROVE or DENY):
- APPROVE emergency +2 GPU reallocation to pool-3 for 6 hours
- APPROVE one-time service credit (finance to finalize amount)
- APPROVE procurement fast-path to provision +25% reserved commit pending contract update

If we have sign-off within 30 minutes we expect the customer-facing impact to be contained and a material reduction in 5xxs within the hour. I will coordinate the postmortem and share a detailed RCA within 48 hours.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Escalations | Redwood Inference
